question: After every side of right triangle \(ABC\) is enlarged to 2 times its original length, how does the sine of acute angle \(A\) change?
solution: The enlarged triangle is similar to the original triangle. Angle \(A\) remains unchanged, and the ratio of the opposite side to the hypotenuse remains unchanged, so \(\sin A\) remains unchanged. The value of a trigonometric function depends only on the size of the angle.
